analysis_type: static PE export and call-site review

observed_abi.XMemAllocatePhysicalPages: BOOL WINAPI (UINT64 flags, SIZE_T* in_out_page_count, UINT64* page_token_array)
observed_abi.XMemMapPhysicalPages: void* WINAPI (void* reserved_address, SIZE_T page_count, UINT64* page_token_array)

reference_behavior.allocation: The title passes flags 0x20400000 and an in/out count. The DLL issues NtDeviceIoControlFile with code 0x1500b8 to the xvcmgmt device. The supplied driver calls ZwAllocateUserPhysicalPagesEx with the AWE section handle.
reference_behavior.mapping: The reference export forwards address, count, and token array to NtMapUserPhysicalPages at reference IAT RVA 0x93e8. A null token array is forwarded for unmapping. The title shifts allocation byte sizes right by 16 to form the page count.
reference_behavior.release: The title passes count in RCX and the token array in RDX. The DLL sends device control 0x1500bc. The packaged xvcmgmt driver reaches ZwFreeUserPhysicalPages.
reference_behavior.page_size_basis: Frosty call-site arithmetic uses byte_size >> 16; Microsoft DirectStorage documentation also describes XMem physical pages as 64 KB pages.
reference_behavior.aperture: Title RVAs 0x5762b1e and 0x57658b2 reserve 0x20402000 with profile 0x23 and protections 0x2404 and 0x10404. The reference adds an AWE section handle for profile bit 0x20. The section creation at DLL RVA 0x17cd requests SEC_RESERVE, SEC_64K_PAGES and SEC_PARTITION_OWNER_HANDLE with MemSectionExtendedParameterUserPhysicalFlags=1.
reference_behavior.driver: Packaged xvcmgmt.sys SHA-256 c652b2f797813c93396c9451635291fc329c7915cc98bbdf5c2c2228e16aabb4, allocate/free dispatch RVA 0x1eca/0x1eb3, NT import call sites 0x47e9/0x44ec. XMemMapPhysicalPages and Scatter directly call NtMapUserPhysicalPages and NtMapUserPhysicalPagesScatter.

tuxbox_provider.implementation: Profile 0x23 reserves a host placeholder. Tokens within each allocation batch refer to 64 KiB offsets in a shared, demand-committed section. Contiguous and scatter mappings replace individual placeholders with views of the corresponding offsets. The last unmap coalesces the reservation for VirtualFree.
limitations: Shared mappings provide CPU coherence. GPU page tables, physical Xbox partitions and direct I/O to pages require additional support.
A retail console success run is unavailable. A stand-in allowed the original Xbox DLL to load on Proton; its real physical-page allocation then failed before returning a token.
